I’m 25 now and a gym instructor, which I love because it’s active and changes every day. But honestly, I can’t keep up with the small stuff. I’ll tell a client I’ll send them a workout plan and totally forget, or I’ll lose my work tablet, keys, even water bottles—stuff I use constantly. It’s embarrassing.

At home, I miss bills, forget to return calls, and sometimes don’t do chores I promised myself I’d finish. It’s not that I don’t care; my mind just drifts. If something sparks my interest—like a new fitness trend—I’ll dive into it for hours. But routine tasks? I tune out. I’ve been anxious lately too, sure—worried about money, relationships—but the distractibility was there since I was, like, nine or ten. When I’m distracted, it’s not because I’m worrying. It’s like a noise, a movement, anything grabs me. I don’t finish tasks not because I’m afraid, but because I lose focus mid-stream.
D002-D011_h023.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D002-D011_h024.question:
I’ve always struggled with staying on top of things, even as far back as grade school—I’d start assignments but rarely finish them, and I’d lose my books or forget to turn in homework. It’s followed me into adulthood. At the bank, I’ll get instructions from my supervisor and start the task, but then I notice something else—maybe a notification on my screen or a coworker walking by—and suddenly I’ve shifted focus and never complete what I was supposed to do. I’m constantly losing my keys, my badge, even my coffee mug. Last week, I missed a doctor’s appointment because I wrote it down but never entered it into my phone.

I forget bills, too—sometimes they sit unopened for days. My apartment’s often a mess because I start cleaning but get distracted. 

I *do* worry a lot—about money, work, my son—but the truth is, I was just as scattered back when life felt simple. The forgetfulness and disorganization don’t come from worrying—they come from my mind jumping to whatever’s new or interesting. I’ll fidget at my desk, tapping my pen or spinning in my chair, not because I’m anxious, but because I’m bored or pulled toward something else.
D002-D011_h024.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D002-D011_h025.question:
I’ve always struggled with staying on top of things, even as far back as elementary school—I remember constantly losing my homework or forgetting to turn it in, no matter how hard I tried. Now, in my third year of the PhD program, it’s getting worse. I’ll read a page of my thesis and realize I have no idea what it said because I got distracted by a notification or just started thinking about something unrelated. I don’t ignore tasks out of laziness—I start them, but rarely finish. Last week, I left my laptop at a café, and just yesterday I missed a bill payment because I forgot to schedule it, even after setting a reminder.

I do feel anxious, sure—especially about deadlines—but the truth is, my mind drifts even when I’m not stressed. It’s not that I’m worrying while reading; I’m just… elsewhere. I get pulled toward things that spark my curiosity, like a new paper or idea, and then I lose track of what I was supposed to be doing. The distraction comes from the outside world, not from rumination. I’ve been like this since I was a kid, long before grad school stress ever started.
D002-D011_h025.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
